messages:
kevin: quick proposal — introduce \"alert credits\" per-route that throttle/shape notifications based on a combo of SLO burn and estimated notification cost. sketch below. thoughts?

sylvie: interesting. concerned about UI complexity and support overhead. can we keep the UX simple? :thinking_face:

kevin: posted quick config sketch:
```json
{
  "alert_credits": {
    "window": "24h",
    "budget": 10,
    "slo_weight": 0.6,
    "cost_weight": 0.4,
    "fallback": "escalate"
  }
}
```

mari: how do credits get consumed? per-notify request, per-alert event, or per-minute? need clear semantics.

kevin: plan is: credits are consumed per routed notification. consumption = normalize(token_cost * cost_weight + slo_burn_rate * slo_weight). so a noisy high-cost model uses more credits.

jonathan: that requires better telemetry. we need realtime token-cost per route and a per-SLO burn metric. do we already emit those at the granularity we need?

sylvie: we have token sampling and per-tenant SLO signals, but not per-route dispatch cost tagged on notify events. we'll need an infra change.

ops-bot: heads-up: this changes the notify API surface (notify_policy -> alert_credit_policy). will impact integrations.

elaine: console UX idea: show a small \"credits remaining\" pill on the SLO card and a sparkline of projected burn. provide a \"top up\" or \"pause\" action. keep defaults sane.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: rollout v2-alerting to canary-2 completed (2025-06-03T02:14Z). observed +14% alert volume in canary window.

mari: edge case — if many tenants spike concurrently, credits could mask systemic incidents. we need an emergency reserve that bypasses credits.

kevin: agreed. add `emergency_override: true` to policy that always escalates for high-severity incidents.

jonathan: API ergonomics: rather than exposing numeric \`slo_weight\`/\`cost_weight\`, expose a \`mode\` enum: \`cost-aware\` | \`slo-first\` | \`balanced\`. simpler for tenants. backend maps mode -> weights.

sylvie: +1 for \`mode\`. UX is easier and the defaults guide users.

kevin: implementation notes: 1) start with a server-side simulator to model historical behavior with credits, 2) require the serving runtime to emit `route_token_count` and `alert_cost_estimate` per notify, 3) console shows projection and a simple mode toggle.

elaine: action items: 1) eng-runtime: emit `route_token_count` and `alert_dispatched` events (jonathan), 2) eng-platform: API proto + console mock (sylvie, mari), 3) data team: run simulation over last 90d to estimate typical credit consumption (kevin).

jonathan: will add a Prom gauge `route_token_cost_per_min{route=...}` and an event stream `alert_dispatched{route, cost_estimate, severity}`.

mari: will mock console card and a compact "quiet-pulse" toggle for on-call to temporarily lower noise during known maintenance windows.

kevin: sounds good. sync tomorrow 11:00 PT to review RFC and simulation plan. @sylvie can you create a short RFC?

sylvie: yep, filing RFC as `docs/alert-credits-rfc.md`. will include API sketches and UX mock links.

elaine: one more UX ask — show projected cost impact if user switches to \`cost-aware\` mode (tooltip: \"estimated token savings / month\").

kevin: nice, helps customers decide.

mari: nit: ensure the console clearly indicates when credits are the reason an alert was suppressed (so on-call knows it's not lost). small toast linking to incident details.

ops-bot: reminder: any API change needs migration plan and deprecation window. create a migration path for `notify_policy` -> `alert_credit_policy`.

kevin: noted. i'll draft migration notes in the RFC.

sylvie: thanks all. will have RFC up by EOD today and schedule the sync. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary signal: if crediting is enabled in canary, we should monitor missed critical alerts metric. tagging ops.

kevin: agreed — add a canary guard: if missed_critical_alerts > 0 for 5m, auto-disable credits and revert to full notify.

jonathan: will add that guard to the runtime canary harness.

kevin: good convo. meeting tomorrow to finalize scope.
